question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi> </mi><mover accent="true"><mi>c</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></math> be three vectors such that the projection vector of <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> on <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="|" open="|"><mover accent="true"><mi>a</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></mfenced></math> . If <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> is perpendicular to <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover></math> , then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="|" open="|" separators="|"><mover accent="true"><mi>b</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></mfenced></math> is equal to:

solution.text:
Since a→+b→ is perpendicular to c→, hence

a→+b→·c→=0

⇒a→·c→+b→·c→=0

⇒5+1+2+5b1+b2 +2=0

⇒5b1+b2=-10       ...1 

Given,

b→·a→a→=a→

∵p→=ri^+sj^+tk^⇒p→=r2+s2+t2

⇒b1+b2+2=4

⇒b1+b2=2   ...2 

Solving 1 and 2, b1=-3, b2=5

∴b→=9+25+2=6
